parts.text:
26 What may be used to produce stationary waves?
A
blowing air over the top of an empty bottle
B
making a loud sound near a mountain
C
passing monochromatic light through a double slit
D
passing water waves through a narrow slit

hints: Notice which set-up confines a wave between boundaries so it must travel back on itself, such as the air column inside the empty bottle.
Recall that a stationary wave needs two progressive waves of the same frequency and amplitude travelling in opposite directions to superpose.
Compare reflection inside a bottle with an echo from a distant mountain, fringe formation at a double slit, and spreading at a single narrow slit.
walkthrough: Identify the condition for a stationary wave: superposition of two identical progressive waves travelling in opposite directions to give fixed nodes and antinodes.
Consider blowing air over the top of an empty bottle: it sets the air column vibrating and the sound wave reflects repeatedly between the open top and the closed bottom of the bottle.
The forward and reflected sound waves have the same speed, frequency and approximately the same amplitude, so they superpose to form a stationary wave with a node at the closed end.

Check the other cases: a mountain echo is a single reflection that travels away, double-slit light is interference of two waves travelling in the same general direction, and a narrow slit gives diffracted travelling water waves.
Only the confined air column in the bottle sustains continuous opposite superposition and resonance. This is option A.

A.explanation: Blowing excites air in the bottle which reflects at the closed bottom, so incident and reflected waves of same frequency superpose to form a stationary wave.

B.explanation: Sound near a mountain produces a reflected echo, but the waves are not confined and continuously superposed in opposite directions to form nodes and antinodes.

C.explanation: Double-slit light produces a two-source interference pattern of fringes, not a stationary wave with nodes formed by oppositely travelling waves.

D.explanation: Water waves through a narrow slit spread by diffraction into a single travelling wave, not two identical oppositely travelling waves.
